title: Finite condensed realization and native tensor normalization
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. Write $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $C_E$ for the raw rational finite stage [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], $B_E$ for the bounded constructible condensed $E$ category [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and $c_E:B_E\to B_\Omega$ for condensed scalar extension. Let $H$ be the actual derived equivalence obtained by native scalar forgetting and restriction along the composite of globalCoefficientIso [def-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-coefficient-construction] with the bounded-to-native coefficient isomorphism. There exist full faithful functors $F_E:C_E\to B_E$ and natural isomorphisms $\beta_h:F_E T^{\rm cond}_h\cong T^{\rm raw}_h F_L$ for every $h:E\subset L$. For every source pair $A=(E,A_E)$ there is $e_A:H(D.JA)\cong c_E(F_E A_E)$. Write $a_h:T^{\rm cond}_h c_L\cong c_E$ for the standard condensed tensor associator. For $A=(E,A_E)$, $B=(F,B_F)$, a common extension $M$ and $f:T^{\rm raw}_{E,M}A_E\to T^{\rm raw}_{F,M}B_F$, these comparisons satisfy $$H(D.J([M,f]))=e_A\,\bigl(a_{E,M}^{-1}\,c_M(\beta_{E,M}F_M(f)\beta_{F,M}^{-1})\,a_{F,M}\bigr)\,e_B^{-1}.$$ Composition is written from left to right and underlying ambient morphisms are understood. This asserts the finite realizations and their tensor normalization; it asserts no bijection on Hom sets of the common-stage category and no essential-image statement at $\Omega$.

proof.text: Construct the ring map from the condensed closure coefficient to the native abelian coefficient as globalCoefficientIso followed by padicAlgClSheafToAdicConstantSheaf. Both factors are isomorphisms. Compose native scalar forgetting with restriction along this map, then derive the resulting additive equivalence. This is the actual H in the statement, defined without choosing data from an existence theorem.

For every finite E use the normalized integral-identity rational equivalence, then continuous rational realization. Encode the continuous E-valued section modules as internal condensed E-modules by the canonical section-ring equivalence. The finite realization preserves bounded locally finite free cohomology and is full and faithful. The auxiliary finite-field datum in the identity comparison is arbitrary and puts no base-field condition on X: choose an auxiliary prime different from ell. For E contained in L use the inverse-completion scalar comparison and the balanced continuous tensor comparison. The internal/section scalar adjunction identifies this with the displayed condensed scalar comparison beta_h; all coefficient maps are pinned on continuous functions.

The finite scalar inclusion followed by the map to the native coefficient evaluates a function by the specified embedding E to the closure. The rationalInclusion_normalized clause of D gives the same map. The integral_residues clause and finite quotient projections identify the completed integral maps. Thus D.integral and balanced derived tensor transitivity give a natural comparison on the integral source. Extend the comparison through raw scalar localization: it is natural on numerator arrows; the uniformizer maps are inverted by both functors, so naturality holds on their inverses and on fractions. Its component at the finite representative A is e_A.

On integral objects, apply D.common_field and the internal/section tensor comparison to identify D of isoToStage with the inverse condensed scalar associator followed by beta_h. Both sides are natural in the rational source, so the equality extends across localization just as in the preceding step. A common-stage representative is isoToStage followed by the inclusion of its stage arrow followed by the inverse isoToStage. Functoriality and naturality of the finite comparison yield the representative equation. This uses no closure Hom descent or essential-image conclusion. Identity extensions, repeated fields and zero objects use the same unit and inverse formulas.
